item.stem: Which characteristic distinguishes a ghazal from a simple love poem?
options: It is just any poem about love and separation.
It uses a strict meter and rhyme scheme throughout.
The form uses couplets with a repeating rhyme+refrain scheme.
It only consists of a single, continuous narrative.
item.explanation: Topic alone is not enough; the form uses couplets with a repeating rhyme+refrain scheme and equal line lengths. This structural pattern is key to identifying the ghazal form.

item.stem: If you are analyzing a ghazal, what structural element must you look for in the second lines of subsequent couplets?
options: Every line must end with the same rhyme and refrain.
The poem must follow a strict iambic pentameter.
The first couplet sets a scheme of a rhyme followed by a refrain.
The final couplet must contain the poet's signature.
item.explanation: The refrain/rhyme scheme is introduced in the first couplet, then repeated in the second line of later couplets. This repetition defines the ghazal structure.

item.stem: Given a four-line stanza, how would you apply the ghazal's structural rules to ensure it adheres to the form?
options: Ensure all four lines have different lengths and no rhyme.
Make the first line the refrain and the subsequent lines unrelated.
Structure it as two couplets, ensuring the first couplet sets the rhyme and refrain.
Use only simple declarative sentences without emotional depth.
item.explanation: Structure it as two couplets, ensuring the first couplet sets the rhyme and refrain. This directly applies the core structural requirements of the ghazal form.

item.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes the ghazal form from a simple love poem?
options: A ghazal is just any poem about love and separation, with no formal constraints.
A ghazal uses autonomous couplets with a repeating rhyme and refrain scheme and equal line lengths.
A ghazal must have a fixed meter and each couplet must share the same theme.
A ghazal is a poem of at least fifteen couplets on the theme of separation.
item.explanation: The topic alone is not enough; the ghazal form uses couplets with a repeating rhyme+refrain scheme and equal line lengths, unlike a mere love poem.

item.stem: How does the rhyme and refrain pattern work in a ghazal?
options: Every line must end with the same rhyme and refrain throughout the poem.
The first couplet sets a rhyme and refrain scheme that is repeated only in the second line of later couplets.
The refrain is used in the first line of each couplet, and the rhyme varies.
Each couplet has its own independent rhyme scheme.
item.explanation: The refrain and rhyme scheme is introduced in the first couplet, then repeated in the second line of later couplets, not every line.

item.stem: An aspiring poet writes a ghazal with eight couplets, each couplet ending with the word 'night' as a refrain, and the first couplet uses 'light' as the rhyme. Which line of the fourth couplet should contain the refrain?
options: The first line of the fourth couplet.
The second line of the fourth couplet.
Both lines of the fourth couplet.
Neither line, because the refrain appears only in the first couplet.
item.explanation: In a ghazal, the refrain appears in the second line of each subsequent couplet after the first. So the fourth couplet's second line has 'night'.

item.stem: A classmate says a ghazal is defined because every line must end with the same rhyme and refrain. What correction is best?
options: Only second lines after the opening couplet carry the refrain.
Every line must rhyme and repeat the refrain.
It must have exactly fourteen lines.
It needs a fixed metrical pattern in English.
item.explanation: The refrain and rhyme scheme is introduced in the first couplet, then repeated in later couplets' second lines. So every line does not end the same way; the pattern is selective, not universal.

item.stem: Which feature would make a poem most clearly identifiable as a ghazal?
options: Five to fifteen couplets, autonomous, equal-length lines, signature last couplet.
Exactly three quatrains and a title.
A strict sonnet meter with no refrain.
One continuous narrative with linked stanzas.
item.explanation: A ghazal is made of at least five couplets, usually no more than fifteen. Its couplets are autonomous, the lines are equal in length, and the final couplet often carries the poet's signature.

item.stem: When scanning a line of poetry, which statement best describes the nature of scansion?
options: Scansion is an objective procedure that always yields one correct pattern.
Stress can sound different to different readers, so scansion is partly interpretive.
A foot must always align with whole words.
Scansion is purely mechanical and requires no subjective judgment.
item.explanation: Stress can sound different to different readers, so scansion is partly interpretive. This acknowledges that scansion is not purely mechanical. It involves subjective judgment about where the stress falls in the metrical pattern.

item.stem: Consider a line where the metrical pattern suggests a trochaic foot. Which statement correctly describes how feet relate to words in scansion?
options: A foot must always align with whole words.
Feet can break across word boundaries and even within a word in scansion.
Scansion is an objective procedure that always yields one correct pattern.
The number of syllables in a foot is always exactly three.
item.explanation: Feet can break across word boundaries and even within a word in scansion. This is because the metrical structure dictates the pattern, not strict word division. This shows how feet interact with the text.

item.stem: Scan the following line: 'The wind blows cold and sharp.' Identify the metrical feet and mark the stressed and unstressed syllables.
options: unstressed, stressed, unstressed, stressed
stressed, unstressed, unstressed, unstressed
unstressed, unstressed, stressed, unstressed
stressed, stressed, unstressed, unstressed
item.explanation: The line scans as unstressed, stressed, unstressed, stressed. This pattern clearly shows the metrical feet within the line. This is a direct application of scansion rules.

item.stem: Which statement about scansion is correct?
options: Scansion always yields one correct pattern because it follows strict rules.
Scansion is purely mechanical and never involves interpretation.
Scansion is partly interpretive because stress can sound different to readers.
Scansion requires all feet to align with word boundaries.
item.explanation: Scansion is partly interpretive because stress can sound different to readers. It is not purely objective. Different readers may scan the same line differently.

item.stem: Which statement about feet in scansion is true?
options: A foot must always align with whole words to be valid.
Feet can break across word boundaries and even within a word.
Feet cannot contain less than two syllables.
Feet must always contain exactly three syllables.
item.explanation: Feet can break across word boundaries and even within a word in scansion. A foot does not have to align with whole words.

item.stem: For the line 'Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?', which scansion is correct?
options: iamb, iamb, iamb, iamb, iamb
trochee, iamb, iamb, iamb, iamb
iamb, trochee, iamb, iamb, iamb
spondee, iamb, iamb, iamb, iamb
item.explanation: The line consists of five iambs: each foot has an unstressed syllable followed by a stressed syllable.

item.stem: A student scans a poem and claims only one pattern is possible because the method is objective. Which response best applies scansion principles?
options: Scansion is objective procedure that always yields correct pattern.
Stress can sound different, so scansion is partly interpretive.
Every foot must align with whole words in poetry.
Feet always contain four syllables in metrical verse.
item.explanation: Stress can sound different to different readers, so scansion is partly interpretive. The marks help show unstressed and stressed beats, but judgment still matters. There is not always one objective pattern.

item.stem: While marking a line, a classmate insists each foot must stay inside whole words. Which correction fits scansion best?
options: A foot must always align with whole words.
Feet can break across word boundaries and within a word.
Scansion uses only rhyme, not stress patterns.
Feet always contain exactly three syllables.
item.explanation: Feet can break across word boundaries and even within a word. Scansion is not limited by whole-word boundaries when showing stress patterns. The goal is to mark metrical feet accurately.

item.stem: Which scansion choice best fits a line with alternating unstressed and stressed beats?
options: Mark the line with stress symbols on the beats.
Ignore stress and count only syllables.
Force every foot to match a single word.
Assume every foot has four syllables.
item.explanation: Standard scansion symbols mark unstressed and stressed beats in the line. Since feet are built from syllables and stress, marking the beats is the right application. The pattern is guided by meter, not by syllable count alone.

item.stem: Which statement about rhyme scheme is correct?
options: Rhyme scheme only applies to poems with perfect end rhymes.
Rhyme scheme can include internal and slant rhymes.
Rhyme scheme is only used in free verse.
Rhyme scheme is unrelated to sound patterns.
item.explanation: The text discusses rhyme patterns and also notes slant rhyme and internal rhyme as meaningful patterning. Rhyme scheme notation applies to any regular pattern, not only perfect end rhymes.

item.stem: Which of the following is true about rhyme in free verse?
options: Free verse never uses rhyme.
Free verse often uses internal rhyme.
Free verse only uses end rhyme.
Free verse avoids all rhyme.
item.explanation: The text says rhyme is elemental in free verse and is more likely internal. Thus free verse does use rhyme, typically internally.

item.stem: If a poet uses the word 'moon' in the middle of one line and 'soon' in the middle of the next, what type of rhyme is this?
options: End rhyme
Internal rhyme
Slant rhyme
Eye rhyme
item.explanation: The text indicates that in free verse, rhyme is more likely internal. Since the rhyming words appear within lines rather than at the ends, this is internal rhyme.

item.stem: When designing a visual sequence for a short story, which technique most effectively uses the language of images to convey mood?
options: Use dense paragraphs to communicate complex plot information.
Employ stark contrasts in lighting and color to establish a somber mood.
List all the characters' emotional states in a bulleted format.
Write a detailed summary of the setting's historical facts.
item.explanation: The section contrasts informational genres with creative writing, emphasizing that images are central to reader experience in fiction and poetry. Employing stark visual contrasts effectively communicates mood, whereas the other options focus too much on factual information.

item.stem: You are writing a passage about a crowded marketplace. To maximize reader engagement, which technique should you prioritize?
options: Focus on the economic theories behind the market's success.
Describe the smells of spices, the sounds of haggling, and the textures of fabrics.
Provide a bulleted list of all vendors present.
Explain the historical significance of the marketplace.
item.explanation: Strong image-making depends on significant, concrete detail that stimulates the reader’s senses. Specificity increases effectiveness: the more specific the image, the better the reader’s sensory and emotional engagement tends to be.

item.stem: Which of the following best reflects a key idea about effective image-making in writing?
options: Abstract statements about emotions are as engaging as concrete description.
Concrete sensory details more directly engage the reader's senses than abstract statements.
Emotional engagement is independent of the specificity of images.
General descriptions are more effective because they allow reader interpretation.
item.explanation: The passage shows that concrete sensory detail more directly engages the senses and sensibilities.

item.stem: Which example best demonstrates the use of language of images to evoke sensory experience?
options: He was very sad.
The room was messy.
The rusty gate screeched as the wind rattled its loose chain.
She thought about her childhood memories.
item.explanation: Option C uses specific concrete details that stimulate the reader's senses, embodying the language of images.

item.stem: A writer wants readers to picture a storm at sea. Which sentence best uses the language of images?
options: The storm was frightening and powerful.
The sea turned slate-gray, and salt spray stung the crew’s faces.
Storms often create fear in sailors.
The scene showed intense weather conditions.
item.explanation: Writers describe what the speaker sees so readers can translate words back into images. Specific, concrete detail makes the image more vivid and engaging.

item.stem: A programmer writes the line x = x + 1 in Python. What is the correct outcome of this statement?
options: The statement is a mathematical equation and it is impossible.
The program will raise a syntax error because of the assignment.
The value of x is incremented by one and the new value is stored in x.
x remains unchanged because assignment is not mathematical equality.
item.explanation: In Python, = is assignment, not equality; the right side is evaluated first and the result is bound to the name on the left. This assignment simply increases x by one.

item.stem: If a variable y is set to y = x + 2, and initially x is 3, what is the value of y after this operation?
options: y will be 5, and this value will update if x changes later.
y will be 3, because assignment only copies the initial value of x.
y will be 5, and this value stays 5 even if x changes afterward.
The operation is invalid because the variable stores an expression.
item.explanation: Assignment stores the value computed at that moment; if y = x + 2 runs when x is 3, y is 5 and stays 5 even if x changes afterward.

item.stem: Given the Python assignment x = 10, and then the operation x = x * 2, what is the final value of x?
options: 10, because assignment only copies the initial value of x.
20, because the right side is evaluated first and the result is bound to x.
100, because the variable stores the expression itself.
An error occurs because the variable name contains a digit.
item.explanation: The right side is evaluated first and the result is bound to x. Therefore, x is first 10, then 20, and the final value of x is 20.

item.stem: What does the statement x = x + 1 do in Python?
options: It creates an impossible mathematical equation.
It assigns x the value of x plus 1, increasing x by 1.
It checks if x equals x+1 and returns False.
It adds 1 to x and prints the result.
item.explanation: In Python, assignment is not equality; the right side is evaluated first, then the result is bound to the name on the left. So x = x + 1 simply increases x by 1.

item.stem: What is the value of y after running y = x + 2 with x = 3, and then changing x to 5?
options: 5, because y stores the expression x+2.
7, because y recalculates when x changes.
5, because the assignment computed 3+2 at that moment.
7, because y equals x+2 as an equation.
item.explanation: Assignment stores the value computed at that moment. When y = x + 2 runs with x=3, y becomes 5 and stays 5 even if x changes afterward.

item.stem: Which of the following variable names is valid in Python?
options: _myVar
2ndPlace
my-var
my var
item.explanation: Variable names can contain letters, digits, and underscores but cannot start with a digit or contain spaces or hyphens. _myVar starts with an underscore, which is allowed.

item.stem: Which variable name is valid in Python?
options: 2total
total_2
Total name
total-name
item.explanation: A variable name may contain letters, digits, and underscores, and it cannot start with a digit. total_2 fits those rules, unlike names starting with digits or using spaces and hyphens.

item.stem: Students assume diamond cannot be scratched or broken because it is the hardest mineral.
options: A) Diamond has low toughness and is easily fractured.
B) Diamond is the hardest mineral, so it cannot be scratched.
C) Diamond is tough, unlike softer minerals.
D) Diamond's hardness measures its ability to withstand impact.
item.explanation: Hardness measures scratch resistance, not toughness; diamond tops the Mohs scale yet has perfect cleavage and can be split by a sharp blow along those planes.

item.stem: If you need to identify an unknown rock sample, which combination of tests should you use for the most reliable identification?
options: Observe the surface color and assume it accurately identifies the mineral.
Test the hardness, cleavage, and streak to identify the mineral more dependably.
Look for impurities and use the surface color alone to identify it.
Analyze the mineral's color alone, as it is the most unique property.
item.explanation: The surface color is unreliable because it varies with impurities. To identify a mineral dependably, you must test its properties like hardness, cleavage, and the streak. These tests help you identify the mineral more reliably.

item.stem: Given a sample of quartz, which property should a geologist use to determine if it will break along flat planes?
options: Measure the mineral's luster to see how it reflects light.
Determine the streak to see the color of its powder.
Observe the cleavage to see if it breaks along flat planes of weak bonding.
Test the hardness against a known standard like a steel nail.
item.explanation: Observe the cleavage to see if it breaks along flat planes of weak bonding. Cleavage is the tendency of a mineral to break along flat planes of weak bonding. This property directly indicates how the mineral will fracture.

item.stem: A mineral looks red in hand, but its powder is white when rubbed on a streak plate. What is the best identification clue?
options: Use the surface color only.
Use the streak color.
Use the mineral's luster only.
Use cleavage only.
item.explanation: Color is unreliable because impurities can change it. Streak, the powder color, identifies a mineral more dependably than the color of the whole specimen.

item.stem: Consider the system of linear equations: x + y = 1 and x + y = 3. Which statement best describes the nature of this system?
options: The system has exactly one unique solution.
Every system of equations has a solution.
The system is inconsistent because the equations describe parallel lines that never meet.
The system has infinitely many solutions.
item.explanation: A system like x + y = 1 and x + y = 3 is inconsistent: the equations describe parallel lines that never meet. This means there is no pair of values for x and y that satisfies both equations simultaneously.

item.stem: If a system of linear equations has two distinct solutions, what can you conclude about the number of solutions?
options: The system has exactly one unique solution.
The system has some finite number of them.
The system has infinitely many solutions.
The system is inconsistent.
item.explanation: Over the real numbers, once a linear system has two distinct solutions it has infinitely many, because the whole line through the two solutions solves the system. This demonstrates the nature of solutions when dependency exists.

item.stem: Use row reduction to determine the number of solutions for the system: 2x + y = 5 and 4x + 2y = 10.
options: The system has no solution.
The system has exactly one solution.
The system has infinitely many solutions.
The system has exactly two solutions.
item.explanation: Row reducing the augmented matrix leads to a row of zeros, indicating that the equations are dependent. This results in infinitely many solutions because one equation is a multiple of the other.

item.stem: Which statement about a system of linear equations is true?
options: Every system of equations has a solution because lines always intersect.
A system with no solutions is called consistent.
A linear system can have exactly two solutions.
An inconsistent system has no solution.
item.explanation: Option A is false. For example, the system x+y=1 and x+y=3 is inconsistent; the equations describe parallel lines that never meet. Option B is false because a system with no solutions is inconsistent, not consistent. Option C is false because a linear system cannot have exactly two solutions (only 0, 1, or infinitely many). Option D is true: an inconsistent system by definition has no solution.

item.stem: Which statement about a system of linear equations is correct?
options: If a system has more than one solution, it has some finite number of them because you can count the solutions.
A system with infinitely many solutions has a unique solution.
A system with two distinct solutions must have infinitely many solutions.
A system with no solutions can be made consistent by adding more equations.
item.explanation: Option A is false. Over the real numbers, once a linear system has two distinct solutions, it has infinitely many because the whole line through the two solutions solves the system. Option B is false because infinitely many is not unique. Option C is true. Option D is false because adding equations cannot make an inconsistent system consistent.

item.stem: A system of two linear equations in two variables has the augmented matrix [[1,2,3],[2,4,6]]. How many solutions does the system have?
options: Zero
One
Infinitely many
Cannot be determined
item.explanation: The second row is twice the first, indicating the equations are dependent. Therefore, the system has infinitely many solutions.

item.stem: A teacher writes a linear system as an augmented matrix before row reduction. What is the main purpose?
options: To list the equations compactly.
To guarantee one solution.
To make the system inconsistent.
To change linear equations into nonlinear ones.
item.explanation: An augmented matrix is a compact representation of a linear system. Row reduction is then used to solve it and determine whether it has zero, one, or infinitely many solutions.

item.stem: A trainer wants a dog to perform a complex trick of rolling over. The trainer rewards the dog with a treat every time the dog gets close to the desired position. What is the trainer using to build this complex behavior?
options: Positive punishment to stop unwanted behaviors.
Negative reinforcement to remove a distracting noise.
Shaping by rewarding successive approximations of the target behavior.
Classical conditioning to pair the treat with the roll.
item.explanation: Shaping by rewarding successive approximations of the target behavior. Shaping builds complex behavior by rewarding successive approximations of a target behavior. This technique is used to teach new, complex actions.

item.stem: A student claims that negative reinforcement is the same as punishment. Which correction is accurate?
options: Negative reinforcement is punishment with a negative outcome.
Negative reinforcement increases behavior by removing an aversive stimulus.
Negative reinforcement always decreases behavior like punishment.
Punishment and negative reinforcement both remove stimuli.
item.explanation: Negative refers to removing a stimulus, not badness. Negative reinforcement removes something undesirable to increase a behavior, while punishment of either sign decreases behavior.

item.stem: A student thinks positive means good and negative means bad in operant conditioning. Which correction clarifies the terms?
options: Positive always means good outcomes and negative means bad outcomes.
Positive means adding something and negative means taking something away.
Positive and negative refer to the pleasantness of the consequence.
Positive and negative determine whether behavior increases or decreases.
item.explanation: In operant conditioning positive means adding something and negative means taking something away; either operation can serve reinforcement or punishment.

item.stem: A trainer removes a shock when a dog performs a trick. This is an example of:
options: Positive reinforcement
Negative reinforcement
Positive punishment
Negative punishment
item.explanation: Negative reinforcement removes an undesirable stimulus (shock) to increase the behavior (trick).

item.stem: A teacher removes extra homework when students turn in assignments early. What is the best label for this consequence?
options: Positive reinforcement
Negative reinforcement
Positive punishment
Negative punishment
item.explanation: Negative refers to removing a stimulus, not badness. Here, removing homework increases turning work in early, so it is negative reinforcement. Punishment would decrease behavior instead.

item.stem: A parent takes away screen time after a teen misses curfew. What effect is expected?
options: Curfew-breaking increases because punishment adds comfort.
Curfew-breaking decreases because punishment reduces behavior.
Curfew-breaking increases because negative reinforcement removes screens.
Curfew-breaking stays the same because consequences never matter.
item.explanation: The law of effect says behaviors followed by unpleasant consequences are less likely to be repeated. Taking away screen time is punishment because it decreases the behavior. In operant conditioning, the sign only tells you whether something is added or removed.
